question: In light of the March infringement package, the Commission decided to refer Greece to the ECJ due to its failure to complete the revision of its river basin management plans and flood risk management plans. At the end of 2023, the preliminary second revision of the river basin management plans were published for consultation.

Meanwhile, Greece solicited advice from a Dutch company in order to put together a plan to repair the damage caused by the Thessaly floods. The plan proposes measures and projects that are not included in the Greek draft river basin management plans. At the same time, Thessaly’s Governor presented an agricultural rehabilitation proposal for Thessaly, which includes water management projects.
Bearing in mind that the Thessaly plain is the largest in Greece and is the heart of Greek agricultural production, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
How does it intend to help Greece with its water resource planning, since it seems to be lost in the midst of different and contrasting plans and proposals?
What steps does it intend to take concerning the proposed projects if these are not aligned with the water resource development programmes?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.6.2024) 1. The Commission has indeed decided to open an infringement procedure1 against Greece for failure to communicate its River Basin Management Plans (RBMPs) and Flood Risk Management Plans (FRMPs) in line with the provisions of the Water Framework Directive2 (WFD) and of the Floods Directive3.

There are different ways in which the Commission supports Member States when developing their planning tools. These range from support to administrative capacity4, cohesion policy financial assistance as well as implementation guidance5 developed jointly with Member States and stakeholders in the context of the longstanding Common Implementation Strategy6. 2.
The Commission has no evidence that such regional projects would be in breach of EU legislation or with the RBMP in preparation.

It is relevant to recall that Article 9(2) of the Floods Directive requires that the development of the first flood risk management plans and their subsequent reviews shall be carried out in coordination with, and may be integrated into, the reviews of the river basin management plans provided for in Article 13(7) of the WFD.

The purpose of this provision is to ensure a coherent, synergetic and integrated approach between the different planning tools of water legislation. Upon receiving such plans from Greece, the Commission will check if this has been the case.
1 Infringement case 2022/2191, https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/inf_23_5380 2 Directive 2000/60/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 October 2000 establishing a

framework for Community action in the field of water policy, OJ L 327, 22.12.2000, p. 1–73, as amended by Commission Directive 2014/101/EU of 30 October 2014, OJ L 311, 31.10.2014, p. 32–35. 3 Directive 2007/60/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 October 2007 on the assessment and management of flood, OJ L 288, 6.11.2007, p. 27–34. 4 https://reform-support.ec.europa.
